doc.title: Yusef Lateef — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Today's music, Coltrane and leading a band
title: Why he calls it so-called improv
summary: Improvisation means no preparation, which is untrue of this music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I was going to ask you, you know, you said “so-called improv.” Now–
Yeah. You know what I say that?
Uh, let’s go into that before–

Yeah, the reason I call it “so-called improv,” because one of the definitions of improvisation is “to present something without previous preparation,” and that’s not true in the case of our music. We use, we, we use a lot of preparation to play it. That’s why that word is not correct.
Have uh...now, I’m assuming this is something you present, what you just told me, is there something you present to your students. Are, are they receptive to uh...?
Mmhmm. Yusef on jazz as “so-called improv” music.
